The concomitant variation fallacy is
Option A: attributing the cause of an event to a single cause when the cause is more complicated
Option B: arguing that since two events happened at the same time, one event must have caused the other
Option C: arguing that since one event preceded another event it must have caused the second event
Option D: drawing a conclusion based on sign reasoning when there is not really a direct relationship between the alleged sign and the subject of the conclusion
